summary: Rabbi Soffer discusses the challenge of reconciling the traditional mourning practices of Tish'a BeAb with the modern reality of a thriving, Jewish-controlled Yerushalayim. He examines the halakhic definitions of destruction and foreign rule as established in the Shulchan Aruch and explores how these concepts have been interpreted by various authorities in the 20th century.
questions: How can we recite the prayer of Nacham while seeing a rebuilt Yerushalayim?
Does the definition of a city being in 'destruction' change when it is under Jewish control?
What does the Shulchan Aruch say about tearing clothes when seeing the cities of Yehuda in their destruction?
